mechanisms: bn_compute_wNAF modified-wNAF generation and its OwnedBuf refusal arms
file_dispositions.note: M42-D1: bn_set_all_zero held as_mut(a) and then called bn_get_dmax(a), which built a shared reference over the same object; the padding write then used a unique borrow invalidated by that foreign read. dmax is now derived from the live unique borrow (top == dmax in this representation). bn_get_words' contract now forbids stores through its shared-derived pointer.

mechanisms: BN_kronecker Cohen algorithm and sign conventions
file_dispositions.note: parts() copies both magnitudes, so no borrow escapes and no raw pointer pair aliases. Every refusal answer is the authority's -2; the export is wrapped by guard_ffi.

The reducers delegate to BN_nnmod against the same static constants, which is the authority's own small/negative arm. Selection reads a copied magnitude and a NULL p selects nothing rather than dereferencing.

mechanisms: ossl_bn_rsa_fips186_4_derive_prime CRT construction and MR loop
file_dispositions.note: The cached constant is published once; the losing thread frees only its own object. Every pool slot is null-checked before use; cleanup clears exactly the internally drawn slots and always unwinds the BN_CTX frame. Residual M42-R1 records the shared BN_clear cleansing gap, which is out of this file's repair scope.

mechanisms: CamelliaKey repr(C) layout and size assertions
file_dispositions.note: No memory-safety defect. Camellia_set_key validates both pointers and all three key sizes. Every mode entry now states that the key must be a schedule produced by Camellia_set_key (grand_rounds 3 or 4); a zeroed CamelliaKey is a valid value but not a valid schedule.

mechanisms: CastKey repr(C) layout and size assertions
file_dispositions.note: M42-D2: a negative len was cast to usize, turning the authority's empty signed loop into a huge read of data; the loop now uses a non-negative count. M42-D3: a negative CBC length made l + 8 negative, and its cast to c_uint made n2ln/l2nn read or write far outside the buffers; the partial arm now selects only a 1..7-byte remainder (the authority's out-of-contract whole-block write on a negative length is not reproduced, per section 17). Two regression tests added.
Key and counter reads are bounded by the contract; the byte-wise XOR preserves out == inp; the 32-bit counter advance and the zero-length no-op match the authority's body.

mechanisms: CONF_VALUE header stack and free callback
file_dispositions.note: No memory-safety defect. headers is released on every early return; req_mem and rsp each have one release; a NULL rsp is handled by the item layer. The req->body non-NULL precondition the authority relies on is now stated in the Safety section.

defects_repaired.note: bn_set_all_zero derived a shared reference to the BIGNUM through bn_get_dmax(a) while its unique borrow from as_mut(a) was live, and then wrote through that unique borrow. dmax is now taken from the unique borrow; the empty padding range is unchanged.

CAST_set_key's loop bound was `len as usize`; a negative signed len wrapped to a near-usize::MAX bound and read past data. The authority's signed loop runs zero iterations for a negative len, which is what the non-negative count now does.

CAST_cbc_encrypt's partial-block arm ran for any l != -8; for a negative caller length l + 8 is negative, and its c_uint cast made n2ln/l2nn walk (and write) far outside the caller's buffers. The arm now runs only when l > -8, i.e. a true 1..7-byte remainder.
bn_get_words now forbids stores through its shared-derived pointer; constructing a mutable pointer from a shared borrow was previously an unreported write obligation. Documentation-only.

Every Camellia mode entry now states that the key must be a schedule produced by Camellia_set_key (grand_rounds 3 or 4); a zeroed key is a valid value but would index outside rd_key. Documentation-only.
OSSL_CMP_MSG_http_perform now states the req->body non-NULL precondition the authority's keep_alive read relies on. Documentation-only.

residual_findings.note: BN_clear sets the Vec length to zero without cleansing the limb storage, while the authority OPENSSL_cleanse's d[0..dmax] before setting top = 0. Reachable from rsa_fips186_4's auxiliary-prime cleanup and BN_CTX_get's slot reset. This is not a Rust soundness defect, and repairing the shared BIGNUM owner invalidates the dependent evidence closure, so it is queued for a dedicated BIGNUM shared-mechanism sweep rather than edited here.
